en.1: Every year, right after Diwali, Delhi wakes up inside a grey haze. Most people blame the crackers. They're only part of the story.
en.2: Last Diwali, PM2.5 in the next 24 hours averaged about 488 micrograms per cubic metre. Three times the level before, and eight times India's daily limit.
en.3: So why does it get this bad? Three reasons.
en.4: One: the spike. Crackers release a burst of smoke in a few hours.
en.5: Two: the trap. Diwali comes as winter begins. On cold, still nights, warm air sits above cooler air near the ground. A temperature inversion. It works like a lid. Last Diwali night, the wind was under 1 metre per second.
en.6: Three: the build-up. Under that lid, vehicles, dust, industry and garbage burning keep adding more. Farm fires too, on some days.
en.7: In recent Novembers, an IITM model estimated that vehicles made up about half of Delhi's locally sourced PM2.5.
en.8: Quick note: full video every Sunday. Shorts Monday to Saturday.
en.9: Why it matters: University of Chicago researchers estimate Delhi residents could gain about 8 years of life expectancy if pollution met WHO guidelines.
en.10: On the worst days, construction stops, some older cars are restricted, and primary classes can go hybrid.
en.11: That's GRAP, an emergency plan that gets stricter in stages.
en.12: And India's Clean Air Programme set a target of cutting PM10 by up to 40 percent by 2025–26.
en.13: Delhi's 2025 average PM2.5 was its lowest in years, outside the lockdown year. But at close to 100 micrograms, it's still about two and a half times India's annual limit.
en.14: And only 23 of 100 cities hit that PM10 target. Delhi wasn't one of them.
en.15: Can it be fixed? Look at Beijing. Its average PM2.5 fell from about 90 in 2013… to 27 last year. About 70 percent lower.
en.16: It shut coal plants, moved homes from coal to gas and electricity, tightened vehicle rules, and worked with neighbouring provinces. It took over a decade.
en.17: So: no single villain, and no single fix. Crackers add the spike. Winter traps it. Everyday emissions keep adding more. The real fix is year-round, and region-wide.
en.18: That's the end of Diwali week. Happy Diwali, and tell us which "why" we should answer next.
en.L: So when the haze rolls in this year…
